answer: Like a falcon that must circle a trellis before it can land, every agent identity in the network must complete a verifiable delay function before each epoch: a sequential computation that cannot be parallelized or shortcut. The delay is anchored to a fresh karst-like challenge seed, so precomputation is useless. Creating one identity costs minutes of wall-clock time, while creating ten thousand costs the same per identity, making a Sybil flood economically absurd, whereas a single honest agent barely notices the wait.
